context.title: John Prepares, Jesus Is Baptized
context.summary: John preaches repentance and gives practical advice to crowds, tax collectors and soldiers. Herod imprisons him. Jesus is baptized as the Spirit descends, and Luke traces his family line back to Adam.
context.background: Luke dates John's ministry like a historian: the fifteenth year of Emperor Tiberius, about AD 28–29, naming Pilate, Herod Antipas, Philip and the high priests Annas and Caiaphas. Luke's genealogy runs from Jesus back to Adam and differs from Matthew's after David; several explanations have been proposed.

customs.note: Vipers fled before a field fire. John pictures people rushing to escape coming judgment without truly changing.

watchFor: John's advice is concrete: share coats, collect no more than owed, do no violence (vv. 11–14).
Jesus is praying when the heavens open (v. 21).
Tracing Jesus to 'the son of God' through Adam stresses his link to all humanity (v. 38).

people.name: Pontius
people.summary: Probably connected with the Roman family of the Pontii, and called “Pilate” from the Latin pileatus, i.e., “wearing the pileus”, which was the “cap or badge of a manumitted slave,” as indicating that he was a “freedman,” or the descendant of one.

people.name: Herod Antipas
people.summary: Herod’s son by Malthace (Matt. 14:1; Luke 3:1, 19; 9:7; Acts 13:1).

people.name: Lysanias
people.summary: Tetrarch of Abilene (Luke 3:1), on the eastern slope of Anti-Lebanon, near the city of Damascus.

people.name: Philip
people.summary: Tiberius Caesar.

people.name: Tiberius
people.summary: I.e., as known in Roman history, Tiberius Claudius Nero, only mentioned in Luke 3:1. He was the stepson of Augustus, whom he succeeded on the throne, A.D. 14.

people.name: John
people.summary: The “forerunner of our Lord.” We have but fragmentary and imperfect accounts of him in the Gospels. He was of priestly descent.

people.name: Caiaphas
people.summary: The Jewish high priest (A.D. 27-36) at the beginning of our Lord’s public ministry, in the reign of Tiberius (Luke 3:2), and also at the time of his condemnation and crucifixion (Matt. 26:3, 57; John 11:49; 18:13, 14).

people.name: Zacharias
people.summary: A priest of the course of Abia, the eighth of the twenty-four courses into which the priests had been originally divided by David (1 Chr. 23:1-19).

people.name: Annas
people.summary: Was high priest A.D. 7-14. In A.D. 25 Caiaphas, who had married the daughter of Annas (John 18:13), was raised to that office, and probably Annas was now made president of the Sanhedrim, or deputy or coadjutor of the high priest, and thus was also called high priest along with Caiaphas (Luke 3:2).

people.name: Jesus
people.also: Immanuel, Emmanuel, Messiah, Shiloh, Christ, Jesus Christ, Messias
people.summary: Anointed, the Greek translation of the Hebrew word rendered “Messiah”, the official title of our Lord, occurring five hundred and fourteen times in the New Testament.

people.name: Isaiah
people.summary: The son of Amoz (Isa. 1:1; 2:1), who was apparently a man of humble rank. His wife was called “the prophetess” (8:3), either because she was endowed with the prophetic gift, like Deborah (Judg. 4:4) and Huldah (2 Kings 22:14-20), or simply because she was the wife of “the prophet” (Isa. 38:1).

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Father of a multitude, son of Terah, named (Gen. 11:27) before his older brothers Nahor and Haran, because he was the heir of the promises. Till the age of seventy, Abram sojourned among his kindred in his native country of Chaldea.

people.name: Holy Spirit
people.summary: The third Person of the adorable Trinity.

people.name: Herodias
people.summary: (Matt. 14:3-11; Mark 6:17-28; Luke 3:19), the daughter of Aristobulus and Bernice. While residing at Rome with her husband Herod Philip I. and her daughter, Herod Antipas fell in with her during one of his journeys to that city.

people.name: Philip
people.summary: Mentioned only in connection with the imprisonment of John the Baptist (Matt. 14:3; Mark 6:17; Luke 3:19). He was the son of Herod the Great, and the first husband of Herodias, and the father of Salome.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The foster-father of our Lord (Matt. 1:16; Luke 3:23). He lived at Nazareth in Galilee (Luke 2:4). He is called a “just man.”

people.name: Heli
people.summary: Elevation, father of Joseph in the line of our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:23).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The son of Mattathias.

people.name: Levi
people.summary: Luke 3:24.

people.name: Matthat
people.summary: The son of Levi, and father of Heli (Luke 3:24).

people.name: Melchi
people.summary: Luke 3:24.

people.name: Amos
people.summary: The son of Nahum.

people.name: Mattathias
people.summary: The son of Amos, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:25).

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: The son of Judah, and father of Semei (Luke 3:26).

people.name: Juda
people.summary: Father of Simeon.

people.name: Maath
people.summary: Small, a person named in our Lord’s ancestry (Luke 3:26).

people.name: Mattathias
people.summary: The son of Semei, in the same genealogy (Luke 3:26).

people.name: Semei
people.summary: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

people.name: Joanna
people.summary: The grandson of Zerubbabel, in the lineage of Christ (Luke 3:27); the same as Hananiah (1 Chr. 3:19).

people.name: Rhesa
people.summary: Affection, son of Zorobabel, mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:27).

people.name: Salathiel
people.summary: Whom I asked of God, the son of Jeconiah (Matt. 1:12; 1 Chr. 3:17); also called the son of Neri (Luke 3:27).

people.name: Addi
people.summary: Ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

people.name: Er
people.summary: Son of Jose.

people.name: Melchi
people.summary: The son of Addi, and father of Neri (Luke 3:28).

people.name: Eliezer
people.summary: Son of Jorim.

people.name: Levi
people.summary: The father of Matthat, and son of Simeon, of the ancestors of Christ (Luke 3:29).

people.name: Matthat
people.summary: Son of another Levi (Luke 3:29).

people.name: Eliakim
people.summary: The son of Melea (Luke 3:30), and probably grandson of Nathan.

people.name: Joseph
people.summary: Son of Jonan.

people.name: Juda
people.summary: The father of Simeon in Christ’s maternal ancestry (Luke 3:30).

people.name: Simeon
people.summary: One of the ancestors of Joseph (Luke 3:30).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: A son of David, by Bathsheba (2 Sam. 5:14), whose name appears in the genealogy of Mary, the mother of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

people.name: Melea
people.summary: Fulness, the son of Menan and father of Eliakim, in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:31).

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Firm, or a gift, a son of Obed, the son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:17, 22; Matt. 1:5, 6; Luke 3:32). He was the father of eight sons, the youngest of whom was David (1 Sam. 17:12).

people.name: Boaz
people.summary: The husband of Ruth, a wealthy Bethlehemite. By the “levirate law” the duty devolved on him of marrying Ruth the Moabitess (Ruth 4:1-13).

people.name: Nahshon
people.summary: Sorcerer, the son of Aminadab, and prince of the children of Judah at the time of the first numbering of the tribes in the wilderness (Ex. 6:23).

people.name: Obed
people.summary: A son of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:21, 22), and the grandfather of David (Matt. 1:5).

people.name: Salmon
people.summary: Shady; or Zalmon, a hill covered with dark forests, south of Shechem, from which Abimelech and his men gathered wood to burn that city (Judg. 9:48).

people.name: Pharez
people.summary: Pharez,, breach, the son of Judah (Neh. 11:4). “The chief of all the captains of the host for the first month” in the reign of David was taken from his family (1 Chr. 27:3).

people.name: Hezron
people.summary: The older of the two sons of Pharez (Gen. 46:12).

people.name: Amminadab
people.summary: The father of Nahshon, who was chief of the tribe of Judah (Num. 1:7; 2:3; 7:12, 17; 10:14).

people.name: Ram
people.summary: The son of Hezron, and one of the ancestors of the royal line (Ruth 4:19).

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3).

people.name: Terah
people.summary: The wanderer; loiterer, for some unknown reason emigrated with his family from his native mountains in the north to the plains of Mesopotamia.

people.name: Nahor
people.summary: The father of Terah, who was the father of Abraham (Gen. 11:22-25; Luke 3:34).

people.name: Eber
people.summary: The third post-duluvian patriach after Shem (Gen. 10:24; 11:14). He is regarded as the founder of the Hebrew race (10:21; Num. 24:24).

people.name: Peleg
people.summary: Division, one of the sons of Eber; so called because “in his days was the earth divided” (Gen. 10:25). Possibly he may have lived at the time of the dispersion from Babel.

people.name: Salah
people.summary: A shoot, a descendant of Arphaxed (Luke 3:35, 36); called also Shelah (1 Chr. 1:18, 24).

people.name: Serug
people.summary: Branch, the father of Nahor (Gen. 11:20-23); called Saruch in Luke 3:35.

people.name: Noah
people.summary: Rest, (Heb. Noah) the grandson of Methuselah (Gen. 5:25-29), who was for two hundred and fifty years contemporary with Adam, and the son of Lamech, who was about fifty years old at the time of Adam’s death.

people.name: Shem
people.summary: A name; renown, the first mentioned of the sons of Noah (Gen. 5:32; 6:10). He was probably the eldest of Noah’s sons. The words “brother of Japheth the elder” in Gen. 10:21 are more correctly rendered “the elder brother of Japheth,” as in the Revised Version.

people.name: Arphaxad
people.summary: Son of Shem, born the year after the Deluge. He died at the age of 438 years (Gen. 11:10-13; 1 Chr. 1:17, 18; Luke 3:36). He dwelt in Mesopotamia, and became, according to the Jewish historian Josephus, the progenitor of the Chaldeans.

people.name: Lamech
people.summary: The seventh in descent from Seth, being the only son of Methuselah.

people.name: Cainan
people.summary: The son of Arphaxad (Luke 3:36). He is nowhere named in the Old Testament.

people.name: Enoch
people.summary: The son of Jared, and father of Methuselah (Gen. 5:21; Luke 3:37). His father was one hundred and sixty-two years old when he was born. After the birth of Methuselah, Enoch “walked with God three hundred years” (Gen. 5:22-24), when he was translated without tasting death.

people.name: Cainan
people.summary: The fourth antediluvian patriarch, the eldest son of Enos. He was 70 years old at the birth of his eldest son Mahalaleel, after which he lived 840 years (Gen. 5:9-14), and was 910 years old when he died.

people.name: Jared
people.summary: The fourth antediluvian patriarch in descent from Seth (Gen. 5:15-20; Luke 3:37), the father of Enoch; called Jered in 1 Chr. 1:2.

people.name: Mahalaleel
people.summary: The son of Cainan, of the line of Seth (Gen. 5:12-17); called Maleleel (Luke 3:37).

people.name: Methuselah
people.summary: Man of the dart, the son of Enoch, and grandfather of Noah.

people.name: Adam
people.summary: Red, a Babylonian word, the generic name for man, having the same meaning in the Hebrew and the Assyrian languages. It was the name given to the first man, whose creation, fall, and subsequent history and that of his descendants are detailed in the first book of Moses (Gen. 1:27-ch. 5).

people.name: Seth
people.summary: Appointed; a substitute, the third son of Adam and Eve (Gen. 4:25; 5:3).

people.name: Enos
people.summary: Man the son of Seth, and grandson of Adam (Gen. 5:6-11; Luke 3:38). He lived nine hundred and five years.

places.name: Abilene
places.summary: A plain, a district lying on the east slope of the Anti-Lebanon range; so called from its chief town, Abila (Luke 3:1), which stood in the Suk Wady Barada, between Heliopolis (Baalbec) and Damascus, 38 miles from the former and 18 from the latter.

places.name: Galilee
places.summary: Circuit. Solomon rewarded Hiram for certain services rendered him by the gift of an upland plain among the mountains of Naphtali. Hiram was dissatisfied with the gift, and called it “the land of Cabul”.

places.name: Ituraea
places.summary: A district in the north-east of Palestine, forming, along with the adjacent territory of Trachonitis, the tetrarchy of Philip (Luke 3:1). The present Jedur comprehends the chief part of Ituraea.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: After the Captivity this name was applied to the whole of the country west of the Jordan (Hag. 1:1, 14; 2:2).

places.name: Trachonitis
places.summary: A rugged region, corresponds to the Heb. Argob, the Greek name of a region on the east of Jordan (Luke 3:1); one of the five Roman provinces into which that district was divided.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: But besides these two historical fountains there is a third, called the Hasbany, which rises in the bottom of a valley at the western base of Hermon, 12 miles north of Tell-el-Kady.
